name: Barnabas
bio: Joses, a Levite from Cyprus surnamed Barnabas ("son of consolation") by the apostles, sold his land and laid the proceeds at the apostles' feet for distribution to those in need (Acts 4:36-37). His far larger role in the early church and alongside Paul is told in detail in the chapters ahead. When Saul, newly converted, tried to join the Jerusalem disciples, they were afraid of him until Barnabas took him to the apostles and vouched for his encounter with the Lord and his bold preaching in Damascus (Acts 9:26-27). Sent by the Jerusalem church to Antioch, where many Gentiles had begun believing, Barnabas rejoiced at their faith and encouraged them to remain devoted to the Lord; he then went to Tarsus to find Saul and brought him back to Antioch, where the two taught together for a year, and the believers there were first called Christians. When the prophet Agabus foretold a coming famine, Barnabas and Saul were entrusted with carrying relief from the Antioch believers to those in Judea (Acts 11:19-30).
